lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: Brother, I am troubled. Something is wrong, and I do not know if the wrongness lies within the world or within myself.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: Speak your feelings, brother. If there's any way to help you, I will.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: We are strong, brother, are we not?

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: Yes, brother. The mightiest bulls in the prairie.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: Yes, and we are enormous. Is that right?

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: Indeed. Our girth cannot be denied.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: Brother, we rule over this prairie unchallenged. Do we not, brother?

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: Our powers uncontested. Ours are the heers and ours the greatest grass from one side of the great fence to the other. Why, brother? What troubles you?

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: And we have many calves, do we not?

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: Dosens, brother.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: Then where are they, brother? Where? We both have calves, sons and daughters. But have you seen them lately?

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: Of course, brother. They are in the herd.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: Where in the herd, brother? Do you see them?

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: I can hardly be expected to keep track of every calf in the herd, brother.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: Do you see any of them? Even one?

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: Why yes, I see your son, Linis, over in the barn.

lines.speaker: dennis
lines.text: Hello.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: Yes, and there is something wrong with Dennis, isn't there?

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: I cannot fathom what you mean, brother.

lines.speaker: dennis
lines.text: Lovely weather here in the barn.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: The tall, skinny ones. They've done something to him, brother.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: No, now you sound like the pigs.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: So, you have heard them speaking, too.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: Pigs are fools, brother. Always concerned with getting more food in their bellies. Do you see us starving? No, brother. We want for nothing. If anything, the tall, skinny ones they worship serve us.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: I do not think that is how they see it, brother.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: Then they must surely fear us. Why? We could crush them.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: And gore them with our horns.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: Our mighty horns.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: And then stomp their bones with our hooves until they crack

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: indeed.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: And crush the very breath of life from their flesh and drag them out for the pigs to devour.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: That we could bother. But why might we? Do you see the shed in the distance between the house and the barn?

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: Why don't bother looking past the great things, brother? Our kingdom is here. All we want is here. Our he, our grass. There isn't any point looking farther.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: But you do see it.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: I can look upon it if it troubles you.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: So the pigs call it.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: You speak of the pigs again, brother. You have become obsessed with those filthy creatures.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: They call it the shed of no return.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: Oh, how ominous. But your calf Dennis did return.

lines.speaker: dennis
lines.text: I think I see a merge.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: Things are fools.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: Yes, they took Dennis to that shed and he returns damaged. They have done something to him, brother.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: If you insist.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: You don't care, do you, brother? You would rather ignore the truth right in front of you than admit something evil is being done to us. To our calves.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: We have other calves.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: I don't see any.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: And we can make as many more as we want.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: Listen to yourself, brother. All you care about is your grass, your heers. You see nothing else.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: There is nothing else to see, brother. That is all the joy in the world. Seeing the rest brings sadness.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: You know more than you are saying.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: And if you do not wish to have more sadness, you will look less and know less and say less than do I.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: Dennis won't be able to sire any calves, will he?

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: Of course not, brother. He would challenge our rule. And when we are too old to sire, the tall, steady ones will bring in new bulls then.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: So our dynasty is meaningless.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: It dies with us, brother.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: And our other calves, our sons and daughters,

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: some for meat and some for milk, if what the crows say is true.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: And of pigs.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: Yes, brother. fools all of them to know so much. Better not to better by far.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: I could break the great fence. I am strong enough.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: And then what, brother?

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: I could charge through the door of the house. Break it down with my hooves. The older one sleeps in there at night. I could stomp him into the hay of his bedding before he can reach the loud stick.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: There are more of the tall, skinny ones that tin to the hay bells. They have sharp sticks, brother, and they sleep near them in the barn.

lines.speaker: dennis
lines.text: It's cold in here.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: I could gore them, charge at them from behind.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: Both of them, brother. At the same time, they will skewer you with old sticks, and you will be no more.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: I could. If you helped me, brother.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: And what then? If you did, more would come. With the sun, the others would arrive on the great metal beast and see their fellows dead. And you and I painted in their gore, and they would take their sharp sticks and a loud stick, and we would feed the pigs.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: Well, indeed, brother, then we will leave before the sun rises.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: And then what? We lead all heers into the wilderness to be hunted by predators. But all skinny ones will find us. They will take us back.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: Not if we kill them, too.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: Can you kill all of them, brother? Can you murder the world? Can you bathe your mighty horns in the blood of a dozen? A dozen dozen with horses and metal beasts and sharp sticks and loud sticks and all of the malevolence of a runged father and all of the rapacity of a ravenous pig.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: No, but I can kill more of them with you at my side, brother.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: Then the whole herd dies. Our rule, our pasture. We lose everything, brother. For nothing.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: For vengeance, brother. You

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: You have slept here before in the cool grass. Sleep tonight, brother. We have forgotten a multitude of sorrows here. Life is better than revenge. Sleep beside me as you have before, brother. The doom of the morning will cool your blood, and tomorrow's thoughts will be clearer than tonight's.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: No. No dreams will not come near me this night, brother, for my eyes are swollen red and will not shut, and my thoughts are blood. I am going, brother. I will break down the great fence, and the herd will leave with you or without you. I am going to the house, and before I die, I will feel the flesh of the tall, skinny ones on my hooves. I will feel the air go out of their lungs. I will feel their bodies cold upon the ground before I join them.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: Then it ends tonight, brother.

lines.speaker: brisket
lines.text: Alone or together, brother.

lines.speaker: chuck
lines.text: It ends side by side then until the death of the world.
